TerraGuard CM

An independent land-evidence platform for Cameroon in which a parcel can be recorded by walking its boundary with a phone and documented by at least ten photographs of the place, every declaration and document receives a dated, salted fingerprint anchored on a public test blockchain, overlaps between declarations are detected in PostGIS before and after registration, and a prospective buyer obtains a rule-based, traffic-light assessment of what the platform knows before payment.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

Under the ordinances of 6 July 1974 and Decree 76/165, the land title is the official certification of immovable property, yet registration remains the exception: most rural and peri-urban land is held under custom, inheritance or long occupation, frequently without any document, and access to the registry is distant, slow and costly. Three failures follow. Holders without papers cannot evidence their own use of the land. The same parcel can be promised to successive buyers, because no shared record of transactions in progress exists before the notarial stage. Family land held in undivided inheritance can be sold by one heir without the others. A prospective buyer therefore pays before any systematic check of competing claims is possible.

02

Contribution

The platform records declarations, not rights, and makes their provenance and conflicts explicit. A parcel is declared through a six-step assistant designed for users without map literacy: boundary capture by walking, by tapping corners or from a surveyor’s plan; a pre-save outline check; four single-tap questions mapped to a declared right (ownership, co-ownership, customary use, occupation, community interest, lease) and a tenure category; at least ten photographs taken in a guided order (approach road, entrance, whole plot, two corners, both limits, both neighbours, a landmark); then a declaration of truth. Documents are stored encrypted and fingerprinted, and integrity can be re-verified against the on-chain commitment. Due diligence on a proposed sale evaluates active reservations, disputes, overlaps, document integrity and configurable authorisation policies; a single exclusive reservation per parcel blocks any competing sale opened on the platform, and a sale by one co-holder is held until the others’ documented consent is recorded. A buyer-facing verdict reduces these facts to green, orange or red with the reasons stated, followed by the four checks that remain necessary off-platform. A guided tour walks visitors through ten constructed cases in ten towns on the live screens.

03

Architecture

A Next.js 16 client and a Fastify API, deployed as two Vercel projects from one repository; the API is packaged with the Build Output API as a single serverless function, and work that a long-running process would do in its worker loop runs after the response through waitUntil. PostgreSQL 18 with PostGIS 3.6 on Neon holds two isolated databases, operational and demonstration, each bound to its own set of contracts. Geometry is validated and reprojected in the database (ST_IsValid, ST_Transform from UTM 32N or 33N), areas and perimeters are computed in metres, and administrative units come from geoBoundaries. Four Solidity 0.8 contracts on Base Sepolia (issuer registry, document-hash registry, parcel-event anchor, evidence-anchor registry) receive only salted commitments and pseudonymous keys; per-environment nonce tracking with resynchronisation on error replaced the library’s nonce manager after a stall was observed. The interface keeps offline field drafts in IndexedDB, reads screens aloud through the Web Speech API, and searches villages through a cached, rate-limited OpenStreetMap Nominatim proxy. Photographs are recompressed in the browser, then re-encoded on the server with sharp (orientation applied, metadata removed, WebP of at most 1,600 pixels with a 480-pixel thumbnail), encrypted under the same envelope scheme as documents, and sealed as a set by a single parcel-event anchor.

04

Method and data

Each phone-captured corner is the accuracy-weighted mean of the fixes received over five seconds (weights 1/σ²), and the parcel’s declared precision is the largest median accuracy among its corners. Overlap detection intersects the current geometry of every active parcel and ignores parcels that merely touch; an overlap is classified as possible measurement imprecision when its mean width, 2·area/perimeter of the intersection, does not exceed the sum of the two declared precisions. The same computation runs without storage on a pre-save endpoint, so the user sees conflicts before committing. Map taps are refused below zoom 15 to prevent implausible vertices, and self-intersecting rings are rejected on the client and again in PostGIS. The verdict is a fixed rule set over platform facts (open disputes, active reservations, blocked sale attempts, competing ownership claims, overlaps beyond margin, failed integrity checks, absent documents, a high review-priority score) and never names a person as a fraudster. Each photograph receives a SHA-256 digest and two 64-bit difference hashes, horizontal and vertical; a photograph in another record counts as identical when the digests match and as similar when both hash distances are at most 6 bits, which recognises a copy recompressed by a messaging application but not a cropped one. A photograph taken with the camera in the preceding three minutes carries the phone’s position, of which only the distance to the parcel is kept: on site within 50 m plus the reported accuracy (capped at 200 m), near within 1.5 km, far beyond. Copied photographs add a risk factor, hold a sale and alert the holder of the original record. The ten tour cases are built through the production services, so the tour displays genuine records and anchors.

05

Verification and limitations

Verification comprised 47 API integration tests against PostgreSQL/PostGIS and a local chain, 12 contract tests, and 11 browser tests, among them the phone flows with the ten-photograph step, the 31-step tour and single-story mode on a 390-pixel screen with basemap tiles delayed by 25 seconds to emulate a rural connection; on the hosted demo, the ten scenarios succeeded and their Base Sepolia receipts were checked. The limits are structural. The platform sees only what is declared on it and cannot block a sale concluded elsewhere; a green verdict is the absence of known problems, not proof of ownership. Phone positions carry errors of several metres, and satellite imagery requires a licensed tile provider. No MINDCAF, cadastre or court system is connected, so the status reserved for official confirmation cannot be assigned. Perceptual hashing does not recognise a cropped or heavily edited copy, the date of a photograph chosen from the gallery is only what the phone reports, and the demonstration photographs are real photographs of land in Cameroon published under free licences on Wikimedia Commons, credited under each picture, which illustrate fictional plots rather than document them. E-mail and SMS delivery are not configured, and the demonstration runs on a test network without monetary value.
